svg.title: Breadth-first search, one step at a time
svg.desc: A step-by-step animation of breadth-first search on the 3 by 3 grid, (0, 0) at the bottom-left, with the center (1, 1) blocked, from S at (0, 0) to D at (2, 2), with the numbers written from D. Step 1: D gets 0 and goes on the to-visit list. Each later step takes the oldest intersection from the front of the list; every open neighbor without a number gets the next number and a place at the back of the list. (1, 2) and (2, 1) get 1; (0, 2) and (2, 0) get 2; (0, 1) and (1, 0) get 3; S gets 4. When the list is empty every intersection has its number. Then the walk downhill from S, one step at a time, always to a neighbor one less: to (1, 0), (2, 0), (2, 1) and D, so the path is [(1, 0), (2, 0), (2, 1), (2, 2)]. The last step explains why it is the shortest: every 1 was written before any 2 and every 2 before any 3, so S's 4 is the fewest steps.
